findings.text: The claim the fence named was not dropped. The figcaption ends 'The raw per-level and per-request values are beside it in local-lane-concurrency-raw.json so the knee can be rederived', and the same assertion stands in the section-4 comment at docs/plans/sn-catalog-audit-instrument.html:951. The raw file carries no per-request values: its levels array holds per-level aggregates (n_requests, wall_s, completed, errors, requests_per_min, agg_completion_tok_per_s, lat_p50/p95/max, starved_over_60s, timeout_rate_900s) and its repeats and rejected_samples hold one row per run, so a reader who opens the file for the per-request figures the sentence promises finds none - the same statement the predecessor's manifest carried, which is how the disagreement was first spotted. Both files were in this node's write fence, and the fence's fourth clause offered exactly two exits: drop the per-request claim, or ship per-request values. Neither was taken, and the node's 20-check gate has no check for it - its 'every request' check covers the SVG footer's 'at 64 every request pays more than 60 s', a different sentence. If the fence meant that footer sentence, then clause four is met and this is a residual of the clause's general half, 'the prose claims only what the raw file contains'; under either reading the sentence is a false claim about the file's contents and the fix is to delete 'and per-request'. It is worth fixing rather than waving through because it is the same defect class the node was dispatched against - a published claim that disagrees with the file it points at - and it outlived a repair whose whole purpose was to remove that class.

The file's own rejected-sample note still frames the c=32 population as three samples: '... the 26.13 reading is a low outlier of the c=32 distribution (three c=32 samples: 36.45, 32.01, 32.98)'. The record now counts four and the band now reads 32% over all four, so the file that the record points to as its authority still carries the three-sample list a reader would take for the sample set - re-deriving the band from the note alone returns the 13% the repair removed. The note is internally inconsistent rather than merely stale, since its own first clause ('a low outlier of the c=32 distribution') places 26.13 inside that distribution. The node deliberately left the raw file untouched and said so, and that restraint is right for measured values; this is a descriptive note, the file was in its write fence, and naming four samples would have left file and record agreeing on the one point the node was dispatched to settle.

The revised prose repeats an unsupported ratio inherited from the raw file's own criterion: 'requests exceeding 60 s - eight times the solo latency' (repeated in the section-4 comment at plan:948 as 'eight times solo latency'), while the file's recorded solo latency is 6.42 s p50, making 60 s 9.3x. The node found and disclosed this itself under follow_ons and framed it correctly as out of its repair's scope, so it is recorded here for completeness rather than as a defect it introduced. Low priority: no conclusion depends on the ratio, and the paragraph around it is otherwise exactly what the file supports.

justifications.durability: 17. The repaired claims live where a future reader meets them - the cumulative evidence anchor, both inside the knee section and as a new section id=knee-record-reconciliation, and the plan's section-4 comments - all committed in one commit that also appends the node's own landing record, so the reconciliation survives without the session. The raw file is preserved untouched as the authority the prose is now held to, which is the right shape for a docs repair: the artifact and the numbers it is measured against are both in the tree. The deduction is that nothing durable keeps them in agreement. The consistency check is /tmp/knee_record_gate.py with its log at /tmp/knee-record-gate.log, neither committed, so the instrument that found these disagreements dies with the machine. That matters more than usual here because the defect class is drift: numbers carried from an earlier draft, silent because prose and file were each individually plausible - 184, 13%, +1.5% and 9% all survived the original landing in one commit - and the next edit to either surface re-drifts undetected. The second residual, the surviving 'per-request values' phrase, is an instance: it outlived a 20-check run because no check covered it. A checked-in document-versus-raw assertion would make the class self-detecting; the fence asked only for the state, so that is recorded as a follow-on rather than charged as a defect.
justifications.evidence: Independently reproduced. I re-ran the node's gate at the committed revision under a header naming that revision, the tree and the command - review_gate_at_c82cae549.log in this run directory, 20 checks, 20 PASS, 0 FAIL, exit 0 - the same 20/20 the manifest reports, now tied to c82cae549 rather than to an uncommitted tree. More useful than the gate, which is the node's own instrument, is that every number it asserts I recomputed from local-lane-concurrency-raw.json myself, and all agree (264; 10.32/31.8925 = 32.4%; (34.30-36.45)/36.45 = -5.90%; 25.5/11.1/22.6%). The gate is not a tautology: its checks are per-claim text assertions over the document, and the manifest records a first run that FAILED the 9% check before the checker's own pattern was narrowed, so at least one of them has been observed red and the discriminating power claim is not vacuous. Two weaknesses in the evidence chain, neither of which moves a number. First, the node's own log at /tmp/knee-record-gate.log carries the mandated first line but names revision 8beb1c4ee - the base - while the content it verified was the then-uncommitted working tree, so from that log a reader cannot resolve which revision's content was checked; the run above closes it by re-running at the commit. Second, the negative control is unarmed for the contracted reason (no test file among the declared write paths) and its compensating discriminating-power claim rests on that unlogged first run. 18.
justifications.fit: 18. House form throughout. The correction is recorded as a reconciliation - a numbered account of what disagreed, in its own section with an r-meta provenance line, plus a plan r-comment carrying data-section/data-who/data-when - rather than silently rewritten into the earlier record, so a reader sees both the original claim and its repair, which is how this plan treats its history elsewhere. The figure is brought into line at all three of its surfaces (header, figcaption, footer) and the figcaption now names the plotted value its delta is measured against, so caption and curve cannot be read as disagreeing. The refusals are the right ones: the knee stays 32, no raw value is edited, and the instrument default plus merged-result verification are explicitly left with the follow-up rather than taken. The corrected section-4 comment now agrees with the earlier measurement comment at line 948 on all four corrected numbers. Two residuals hold it at 18 rather than 20: the surviving per-request phrase in the figcaption and the section-4 comment, and the raw file's rejected-sample note, which still lists three c=32 samples where the record now counts four.
justifications.goal_fidelity: The goal is that the concurrency-knee record agree with the raw measurements it publishes, and on every measured number it now does. I recomputed each from the raw rows at c82cae549 rather than accepting the node's own gate: the nine n_requests rows are 16+16+16+24+32+64 = 168 for the levels, 32+32 = 64 for the repeats and 32 for the mis-dispatched attempt, so 264, and the evidence prose states 264 with exactly that breakdown ('The record carries 264 requests in all: 168 across the six measured levels, 64 in the two c=32 repeats, and 32 in the mis-dispatched attempt held out of the curve'). The four samples the record assigns an achieved concurrency of 32 are 36.45, 32.01, 32.98 and 26.13; their range 10.32 on a mean of 31.8925 is 32.4%, and the record states the definition explicitly ('the range is 36.45 - 26.13 = 10.32 req/min on a mean of 31.89'), with the c=64 point at 34.30 shown lying inside it. The caption delta is (34.30-36.45)/36.45 = -5.90%, a fall, which is the direction the plotted curve actually has. The doublings past 4 from the throughput column are 21.32->26.76 (+25.5%), 26.76->29.74 (+11.1%) and 29.74->36.45 (+22.6%). One point worth recording for the next reader, because it looks at first like a metric switch and is not: the 13% this replaced and the 32% that replaced it are the same statistic, range over mean, computed over three samples versus four (13.1% over 36.45/32.01/32.98), so the widening is attributable to the admitted sample and not to a changed definition. The node also found and fixed a fifth disagreement its fence did not enumerate (the third doubling read 9%, the column gives 22.6% -> 23%). What keeps this at 17 rather than higher is the one claim it left unreconciled: the record still publishes 'raw per-level and per-request values' beside the figure (evidence:1138, plan:951) while the raw file carries per-level aggregates only. That is the same defect class the node was dispatched to remove, and it is the subject of finding 1 below.
justifications.scope_discipline: 20, and verified rather than assumed. `git log --oneline 8beb1c4ee..c82cae549` is a single commit; `git diff --stat 8beb1c4ee c82cae549 -- docs/figures/sn-catalog-audit-instrument/local-lane-concurrency-raw.json` is empty, so the raw file the fence put in scope is byte-unchanged - the right restraint for a measurement input, and what the commit body claims. plan-version '38' and plan-modified '2026-09-21' are identical at base and head, so the meta lines the landing contract protects were not touched. All four f-scai-* followups (layer-one, concurrency-knee, groups-wiring, getattr-aperture) are still data-status='open', so the node did not close its own driving followup. It wrote three of its five fenced paths - the evidence anchor, the figure and the plan - and nothing outside them, in one conventional commit whose subject states the change and whose body states the four disagreements in full; it carries no AI trailer and no plan, sprint or ticket identifier. No branch was created and nothing was pushed. The manifest uses the contracted negative_control_log key with a 'none: <reason>' value, where the predecessor node used a non-contracted key. Worktree clean at c82cae549.
